overview: The Climate Systems Science stream is focused on a broad introduction to the science of the Earth's climate system. Students will gain an understanding of the fundamentals of atmospheric science, oceanography and chemistry and have the option of focusing their studies in areas such as climate and vegetation, hydrology, biology, biogeochemistry or environmental and resource management. Courses are designed to highlight the interrelated nature of climate system components and give students the ability to critically analyse problems in multi-disciplinary science context. Students will also develop an ability to undertake directed research.
clos: ["Describe the processes that govern climate, weather, and extremes, including the dynamics and thermodynamics of the atmosphere and oceans, and their interactions with the terrestrial and cryosphere systems.", "Demonstrate an understanding of the physical concepts, as well as technical and computational approaches used in modelling the Earth system and perform climate model simulations to evaluate hypotheses under various climatic scenarios.", "Explain the impacts of climate change on ecosystems and identify and communicate risk management strategies to mitigate and adapt to climate change.", "Use model output and complex data products to evaluate present and past climates, and project future climate scenarios, including estimating uncertainties under different greenhouse gas emissions and other external forcings.", "Demonstrate deep knowledge of climate systems and the underpinning science spanning physics, mathematics, chemistry, biology, and earth sciences."]

title: Climate Systems Science
overview: The Climate Systems Science stream is focused on a broad introduction to the science of the Earth's climate system. Students will gain an understanding of the fundamentals of atmospheric science and oceanography while having the option of focusing their studies in areas such as climate change and risks, land processes, hydrology, biogeochemistry or environmental and resource management. Courses are designed to highlight the interrelated nature of climate system components and give students the ability to critically analyse problems in multi-disciplinary science context. Students will also develop an ability to undertake directed research.
clos: ["Describe the processes that govern climate, weather, and extremes, including the dynamics and thermodynamics of the atmosphere and oceans, and their interactions with the terrestrial and cryosphere systems.", "Demonstrate knowledge of climate systems and the underpinning science spanning physics, mathematics, chemistry, biology, and earth sciences.", "Use model output and a range of data products to evaluate present and past climates, and project future climate scenarios, including estimating uncertainties under different greenhouse gas emissions and other external forcings.", "Demonstrate an understanding of the physical concepts used in modelling the Earth system and perform climate model simulations to evaluate hypotheses under various climatic scenarios.", "Describe the impacts of climate change on ecosystems and identify risk management strategies to mitigate and adapt to climate change."]

title: Climate Systems Science
overview:
The Climate Systems Science minor provides an introduction to the science of the Earth's climate system. Students will learn the fundamentals of the atmosphere, ocean and land processes, and how these inform our understanding of climate change. Critically, students will learn about risks relating to climate change, how these are predicted and learn to separate fact from fiction, and greenwashing from genuine action. This minor will provide a foundation in climate systems that is relevant and valuable for all science disciplines, and enable students to link their area of speciality to climate change issues. 
 This minor will provide a foundation of climate systems that is relevant and valuable for all science disciplines.
